gates.reason: Directory entries are followed with statSync/readFileSync, allowing a .json symlink to escape the supplied directory.
Checked field validation, entrypoint-based attribution, percentage arithmetic, anomaly counts, and first-seen version provenance.
Default limits leave both entry count and per-file size effectively unbounded during synchronous ingestion.
Test-only synthetic JSON construction has no auth, filesystem, egress, browser, command, SQL, RBAC, or secret-handling surface.
The tests explicitly re-derive the 2.6/3.5 character-density estimates and cumulative per-turn snapshot sums.
Small deterministic unit fixtures are not a shipped or hot-path runtime surface.
Test-only transcript fixtures perform no privileged I/O, egress, rendering, command execution, or secret handling.
Checked assertions for token totals, compaction arithmetic, pricing, thinking residuals, and tool-result attribution against their fixtures.
Unit-test fixtures and assertions do not participate in production ingest performance.
Untrusted JSONL is parsed without eval, command execution, filesystem access, HTML rendering, credential access, or network egress.
Usage fields are trusted as numbers without runtime validation, so malformed transcript values can corrupt token and cost calculations.
Inspected the ingest loop, message deduplication, context accumulation, tool-result joins, reductions, and WeakMap cost memoization; work remains linear in transcript content.

findings.title: Session-registry parser follows JSON symlinks outside the requested directory
findings.what: The parser retains only each Dirent name, then uses statSync and readFileSync on the joined path. statSync follows symbolic links, so a directory entry such as leak.json pointing outside dir is accepted when its target is a regular file and its JSON has the expected fields. This violates the supplied-directory boundary and can ingest unrelated local data.
findings.fix: Retain the Dirent and reject entries for which isFile() is false, then open/read with no-follow semantics where supported and verify the opened file remains beneath the intended directory.
findings.acceptance: Create a temporary registry directory containing valid.json and escape.json as a symlink to a valid registry-shaped JSON file outside that directory; parseSessionRegistryDir must return only valid.json's entry.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that lines 80 and 92-100 neither reject Dirent.isSymbolicLink() nor use lstat/no-follow semantics; statSync follows the link before isFile() is checked.

findings.title: Registry ingestion defaults to unbounded synchronous file count and size
findings.what: When options are omitted, maxEntries normalizes to an effectively unlimited value and maxFileBytes becomes -1, disabling the size check. The parser then synchronously reads and parses every .json file in full, allowing a large or corrupted registry directory to block the process and cause excessive memory use.
findings.fix: Set conservative finite defaults for maxEntries and maxFileBytes, preserving explicit smaller caller limits, and skip files beyond those budgets.
findings.acceptance: With default options, a fixture containing more than the entry budget plus an oversized JSON file must process at most the documented entry limit, skip the oversized file, and complete within the parser's documented latency/memory budget.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass confirmed the default path at lines 79 and 81-86 imposes no practical entry or byte ceiling before synchronous readFileSync/JSON.parse at line 100.

findings.title: Unvalidated usage values can corrupt token totals and cost estimates
findings.what: The parser checks only that usage is truthy, then copies token and request fields without verifying they are finite, non-negative numbers. Since JSON is untrusted at runtime, strings, negative values, or values such as 1e309 can propagate into reductions and pricing, producing concatenated string totals, negative spend, Infinity, or NaN rather than reproducible calculations.
findings.fix: Normalize every usage counter through one helper that accepts only finite non-negative numbers (and clamps/rejects invalid values); also bound cacheCreation1hTokens to the inclusive range 0..cacheCreationTokens before pricing.
findings.acceptance: Add parser tests using string, negative, and 1e309 values for every usage counter; returned counters and estimateCost must remain finite, numeric, and non-negative, while valid counters retain the existing totals and prices.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed there is no runtime numeric validation between the truthiness check at line 243, direct assignments at lines 273-282, reductions at lines 425-429, and arithmetic at lines 478-487.
